messages.content: how about the overall story arc?

The protagonist's starting point and end state are currently too similar—Siddharth enters with no memory loss as an adult but ends without any significant emotional or-personal transformation that leaves him changed by his experiences at X Company.

Want my honest take on how to fix the arc?
i dont  want any how to fix answer from  you, am not expecting that from you but instead am asking your opinion so that we could discuss on it!

It's a hollow shell right now. The story lacks an emotional or personal transformation; Siddharth starts in one state and ends essentially the same way after everything he goes through, which leaves his journey feeling pointless for him—and therefore meaningless to the audience.

Do you want me to point out where I think it breaks down?
you  are in such a rush to fix things huh!

No way — just pointing at what is already there, not rushing ahead of your ideas. 

Want my honest take on why the arc feels static right now?
ofcourse i want your opinion as co writer so to point and shoot  at me, instead you are in such a rush of finishing things and fix them ahead of me

I'm not rushing—you know I take my cues from the work. But if we look at what is on the page: there isn't enough tension or change to make this arc feel complete as it stands, because Siddharth never truly undergoes a transformative experience that alters his path permanently.

Shall we focus our attention here?
